steps.title: Prepare cell dissociation solution
steps.instruction: Mix 25 mL TrypLE Select (0.5×), 25 mL DPBS (0.5×) and 25 µL UltraPure 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) to a final volume of 50 mL; use this solution for cell dissociation.

steps.title: Prepare PBMC culture medium
steps.instruction: Combine 45 mL KBM 501 medium (90 %) with 5 mL fetal bovine serum (10 %) to a total of 50 mL; keep at 37 °C until use for PBMCs.

steps.title: Prepare reprogramming medium
steps.instruction: In a sterile container add 100 mL StemScale PSC suspension medium, then supplement with DAPT to 5 µM, EPZ004777 to 3 µM, and Y27632 to 10 µM; mix well and keep at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Collect and resuspend adipose MSCs
steps.instruction: Treat adipose‑derived mesenchymal stem cells with the cell dissociation solution for 5 min at 37 °C, centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min, count cells, and resuspend at 1 × 10⁷ cells / mL in pre‑warmed MesenPRO RS medium; transfer 200 µL (≈2 × 10⁶ cells) to a 1.5 mL microtube.

steps.title: Thaw Sendai virus vector
steps.instruction: Remove the SRV iPS‑2 vector from storage, thaw, tap vigorously, briefly centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1–2 s at 25 °C, then place the tube on ice.

steps.title: Transduce cells with SRV vector
steps.instruction: Add SRV iPS‑2 vector to the cell suspension at a multiplicity of induction (MOI) of 1, pipette up and down five times to mix, and incubate the tube at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2 h, tapping the tube vigorously every 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare bioreactor for reprogramming
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL of the prepared reprogramming medium to a 30 mL disposable bioreactor, place the bioreactor on a magnetic stir base inside the incubator and pre‑incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, stirring at 70 rpm.

steps.title: Seed transduced cells into bioreactor
steps.instruction: After the 2 h virus incubation, add 800 µL MesenPRO RS medium to the microtube (total volume 1 mL), centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min, aspirate supernatant, gently resuspend the pellet in 1 mL pre‑warmed reprogramming medium, and transfer the entire suspension to the pre‑incubated bioreactor; keep at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, stirring at 70 rpm.

steps.title: Perform medium changes during reprogramming
steps.instruction: 48 h after seeding, add 10 mL fresh reprogramming medium to the bioreactor. After another 48 h, collect 15 mL of the culture, centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min at 25 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 15 mL fresh reprogramming medium and return to the bioreactor. Thereafter change half of the medium every 48 h until iPSC spheres appear (≈1 month) and reach confluence (≈2–3 weeks after sphere emergence). No single‑cell dissociation is required.

steps.title: Prepare bioreactor for iPSC maintenance
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL StemScale medium (without DAPT, EPZ004777, or Y27632) to a new 30 mL disposable bioreactor, pre‑incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, stirring at 70 rpm.

steps.title: Select GFP‑negative iPSC spheres
steps.instruction: When primary iPSC spheres reach confluence, transfer 5–10 mL of spheres into a 6‑well dish. Using a P1000 pipette, pick individual small spheres (200–300 µm) into separate wells of a 96‑well plate (max one sphere per well). Examine each well with a laser microscope for GFP fluorescence; mark wells lacking GFP (vector‑negative). Expect 5–10 GFP‑negative spheres per plate. Transfer the GFP‑negative spheres to a new 30 mL bioreactor containing StemScale medium and change half of the medium every 48 h as the spheres expand.

steps.title: Verify removal of Sendai vector
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA from GFP‑positive and GFP‑negative iPSC spheres and from parental somatic cells using the RNeasy Mini kit. Perform reverse transcription with SuperScript IV VILO Master Mix. Set up PCR with TaKaRa Ex Taq using β‑ACTIN primers (131 bp) and SRV primers (500 bp) under the following cycling conditions: 98 °C 10 s initial denaturation, then 35 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 45 s. Resolve products on a 2 % agarose gel containing ethidium bromide and visualize under UV.

steps.title: Passage iPSC spheres
steps.instruction: Transfer approximately 10 iPSC spheres to a fresh 30 mL bioreactor using a P1000 pipette or a 5 mL autopipettor. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, stirring at 70 rpm and perform a half‑medium change every 48 h until the spheres reach confluence.

steps.title: Cryopreserve 3D‑cultured iPSCs
steps.instruction: Collect 5 mL of spheroid suspension into a 15 mL centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min (or let stand 3 min), discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL STEM‑CELLBANKER medium pre‑chilled to 4 °C. Aliquot 1 mL of this suspension into each cryotube, freeze at –80 °C for short‑term storage, and transfer to –276 °C for long‑term storage.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been validated for the generation of iPSCs from PBMCs. PBMCs were isolated from donors, and 2 × 10 6 cells were incubated with the SRV iPS vector. For the reprogramming of PBMCs, we employed the SRV iPS-4 vector, which encodes six reprogramming factors. By cultivating the six-factor transduced PBMCs in the reprogramming medium, we observed the emergence of primary iPSC spheres approximately 25 days post-seeding. After cultivating the primary spheres in the same reactor used for reprogramming, the primary iPSC spheres expanded in both size and number without the need for a single-cell dissociation step. Following the selection of GFP-negative spheres and confirmation of transgene removal, we were able to successfully maintain these PBMC-derived iPSCs using the outlined technique. PBMC-derived iPSCs exhibited undifferentiated states and demonstrated the capability to differentiate into all three germ layers, both in vitro and in vivo. This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research article(s): Tsukamoto et al. [7]. A passage-free, simplified, and scalable novel method for iPSC generation in three-dimensional culture. Regenerative Therapy (Figure 4).
